builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HerAgent: A Block-Level Checkpointing Harness for Coding-Agent Environment Setup
summary: HerAgent replaces single-command or whole-script progress control with a unified semantic block abstraction for execution, validation, checkpointing, and rollback. It requires implementing a checkpointing harness with block-level state capture, introducing moderate engineering complexity but no additional hardware requirements. Failure can occur if block boundaries are misaligned with actual dependencies or if state capture mechanisms introduce significant overhead.
rationale: The technique uses orchestration and state management rather than large-scale training, fitting constrained infrastructure while substantially improving reliability and reducing costs.

claims.statement: HerAgent replaces single-command or whole-script progress control with a unified semantic block abstraction for execution, validation, checkpointing, and rollback. It requires implementing a checkpointing harness with block-level state capture, introducing moderate engineering complexity but no additional hardware requirements. Failure can occur if block boundaries are misaligned with actual dependencies or if state capture mechanisms introduce significant overhead.
Improves setup success across all comparisons, e.g., 52.0% to 85.0% on Installamatic-Bench and 46.3% to 70.4% on SetupBench; reduces setup costs by up to 94.5%.
